headline: Adobe expects shoppers sent to US stores by AI assistants to more than double this holiday season.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the forecast was released on 28 Sep and this is a late write-up.
importance_line: Shoppers are increasingly letting chatbots choose where they buy, which changes how retailers reach customers and which products get seen, although this is Adobe's own forecast and survey, not measured sales.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Adobe forecasts a 130 percent rise in traffic sent to US retail websites by AI tools this holiday season, far ahead of the 4 percent it expects from paid search and 17 percent from social media, within total online holiday sales of 275.1 billion dollars, up 6.7 percent. The forecast was released on 28 Sep, as Retail Dive reported earlier; Adobe's July survey of 5,000 consumers found 77 percent of AI shoppers felt more confident in their purchases and 69 percent said they were less likely to return items.
notes: Release date from Retail Dive (1 Oct 2026, "released Monday").
